PHASE.NAME: Technology Decision Bootstrap Fix
PHASE.GOAL: Prevent new-project planning from inheriting a fake Rust/Axum/SQLite stack and require an explicit technology decision before implementation.
PHASE.SOURCE_PLAN: MyGRACE reviewer finding after v2.6.7: syn init creates a misleading technology.xml for blank projects.

DATA_FLOWS.FLOW: Blank project init writes a Technology artifact with status needs-decision and no selected language, framework, database, or test runner.
Existing repository technology generation detects manifests and lockfiles before writing concrete exact-version technology choices.
Planning guidance treats needs-decision as an instruction for the LLM to recommend a stack from requirements instead of confirming a bootstrap default.

STEPS.step-1: Split pending decision artifacts from detected exact-version technology generation.
STEPS.step-2: Change syn init bootstrap to write the pending decision artifact for blank projects.
STEPS.step-3: Update grace_plan guidance for pending technology decisions.
STEPS.step-4: Add regression tests that block ghost Rust/Axum/SQLite stack claims in blank project init.
STEPS.step-5: Clarify quick declaration gates versus real hosted coverage and benchmark execution.

RISKS.RISK: Technology validation currently expects concrete exact-version stack sections; pending-decision artifacts must remain valid without weakening validation for generated concrete stacks.
Existing Synapse repository technology.xml must remain concrete and release-valid while new blank projects avoid fake defaults.
